request.spec:
Show on each person their settled-total (the due of their SETTLED claims that count, at
their frozen figures, corrections included) and their open-total (the due of their OPEN and
PENDING claims that count: a held, deferred or retired-and-excluded claim is left out as it is
from the due-total). Show the sheet's settled-total and open-total too, each simply everyone's
figure added up (not trimmed). The two must add up to the person's untrimmed due-total before the
cap.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each person their settled-total (the due of their SETTLED claims that count, at
their frozen figures, corrections included) and their open-total (the due of their OPEN and
PENDING claims that count: a held, deferred or retired-and-excluded claim is left out as it is
from the due-total). Show the sheet's settled-total and open-total too, each simply everyone's
figure added up (not trimmed). The two must add up to the person's untrimmed due-total before the
cap.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person row now shows a settled-total and an open-total, and the sheet shows both totals summed across everyone. All 4 acceptance tests pass in `bin/e2e`.

**How the figures are worked out**
- **Settled-total:** the dues of a person's SETTLED claims that count. It uses their frozen figures, and corrections are included.
- **Open-total:** the dues of their OPEN and PENDING claims that count. Held, deferred and retired-and-excluded claims are left out, the same way the due-total leaves them out.
- **Adding up to the due-total:** both use the same claims and per-claim dues as the person's due-total. Together they make that due-total before the cap.
- **Sheet totals:** everyone's figures added up, with nothing trimmed.

**What changed**
- `src/main/frontend/features/rates/rates.ts`: a new `personSplitTotals` function that works out the two figures for a person.
- `src/main/frontend/features/rates/rates.slot.tsx`: new "Settled" and "Open" columns on each person row, placed after the Due column, plus a "Settled in all / open in all" line under "Due in all".

I didn't change the server, the stored data or the audit records. The app already works out the due figures in the browser, the tests expect no new audit lines, and display-only figures don't need storing.

The new figures are never "n/a": a claim with no figure is skipped. So when a person's due-total shows n/a, their settled- and open-totals add up whatever figures do exist.
